message.content:
A cell that contains more than one nucleus is called a **multinucleated** or **polynucleated** cell.  
In biology this condition is often referred to as a **syncytium**.  

Examples of multinucleated cells include:

| Cell type | Typical function | Where found |
|-----------|------------------|-------------|
| **Osteoclast** | Bone resorption | Bone tissue |
| **Skeletal muscle fiber (myocyte)** | Contraction | Skeletal muscle |
| **Placental syncytiotrophoblast** | Nutrient transfer & hormone production | Placenta |
| **Certain fungal hyphae** | Growth & nutrient absorption | Fungi |

So if you’re looking for a general term, “multinucleated cell” (or “polynucleated cell”) is the correct name.
